issues.what: Inner-fold over-purge for learner B's p* selection (and the same helper used by A): fold_masks purges training trades whose trajectory intersects [min(block start), max(block end)] over the test blocks. For the non-contiguous inner folds `tr_blocks[i::3]` this range spans the blocks in between, so every trade in those blocks is purged and the inner training set collapses to a single block for 2 of 3 inner folds (1m: 250-492 trades instead of the intended ~5 blocks; 5m: 47-82 trades). p* is therefore chosen on badly under-trained inner models. Not a leak (it is conservative), and B is not a candidate, but FINDINGS' 'p* by an inner 3-fold on the training fold' over-states the procedure that actually ran.
issues.evidence: Reproduced: outer fold 0 (1m) inner test blocks [4,7,10] -> inner train n 492 from blocks [11] (intended [5,6,8,9,11]); [5,8,11] -> n 361 from [4]; outer fold 2 [0,3,6] -> n 250 from [7]. 5m: [0,3,6] -> n 47 from [7]; [4,7,10] -> n 82 from [11].
issues.fix: Purge per test block (loop over blocks exactly as harness._purge does) or use contiguous inner folds; re-run 03_b_imitation.py and state the inner training sizes in FINDINGS.

The two give opposite signs for the 1m lead (-67.49 vs +4.01). The verdict does not change (SPA p 0.396 fails either way), but the adapted rule is post hoc and the primary statistic differs from harness.GO.

result.verified: Re-ran independent checks from the scratchpad (nothing under the study, ledger or data written; numba/bytecode caches redirected). IS discipline: all 4452 (1m) / 826 (5m) priced units are IS rows (max SETUP date 2025-12-31), grid entries == study entries, every block >= 0; bars/events/card/zones are indexed only at IS bars (the Jan-2026 contract's last candle enters only as a cap bound, never a price); the harness ledger holds exactly two rows from this study (exit_policy/gate_x_exit, ids ac28bea0c7c26c6f, aee3ef4df479e783). Exact-replay claim confirmed and strengthened: the numba floor equals the lab.manage Foundation-stop-only variant (grid col 1176) on EVERY trade (exit bar identical, max |net diff| 0.0) on both timeframes; a fresh lab.manage call on 300 random trades per tf gives 0 mismatches; every trajectory stays in its entry session (so harness purge by the L1 exit bar is equivalent to purge by the variant's exit); lab.manage's cap is the entry day's 15:25 (lab.py:932-933), matching the FINDINGS cap definition; price_np == lab.price_trade holds on all 4452/826 stop-or-cap fills. Nested OOF rebuilt from the grid via harness.purged_splits reproduces c_pick: 1m mean -923.04, diff 86.57, top-1% gains removed -67.49, top-1% winners removed 4.01, sign-flip blocks p1 0.0149 (10/12); 5m -818.36, -61.31, -204.16, -76.62, p1 0.7454 (5/12). In-sample best = variant 1176 (1m, -904.77, 226 above Foundation) / 1024 (5m, -648.81, 173 above). The top 45 per-trade gains sum to 682,848 INR against a total diff sum of 385,417, so the 'few runners' description is accurate. Learner-B/A states: bars_held, unreal, MFE, MAE re-derived from bars <= k match on the longest trade; STATE_COLS contain no fnd_/l1_/fwd_/fzpos_/fzpost_/final-state field; card read from fz_card as-of; rooms via birth_bar <= k < retired_bar; CHoCH-against via events i <= k; bars_to_sqoff equals clock minutes to 15:25 on 1012/1026 IS 1m sessions (gaps only on 14 truncated sessions, negligible). Thresholds: C = argmax on the training fold (12 purged folds, 66 CPCV splits -> 11 paths); B p* chosen inside the training fold; A has no tuned threshold. Exit ledger: 3173 rows = 3173 unique ids = 3173 vector files (per tf 1568 C + 11 CPCV + 4 comparators + C_nested + C_best_is + B, plus A on 5m). SPA/PBO family = the 1568 C variants; SPA best is variant 785 (stop 75, CHoCH on, t 1.683) -> p 0.396; the nested pick's own session-equal-weighted gain is +31.4 INR/trade (t 0.55, unadjusted one-sided p 0.29), so the family-wide SPA failure is not an artefact. The pre-registered pass rule fails on 1m (SPA, and the study's top-1% variant) and on 5m (nested diff < 0); the null result and 'no candidate' verdict stand.
